01 / 03

An idea lands
in Discord.

Send a task to your private forum. Plompy checks who sent it, saves it to a durable queue, and starts the work on your Linux machine.

!work 30mA goal. A time budget. Room to work.
02 / 03

Your agent.
A whole toolkit.

The saved runner session picks up your instructions and context. Inspect a repository, use a browser, read documentation. You choose the connections.

!goal 30m --repo "/srv/project"Add a fresh Codex supervisor to review the change.
03 / 03

The result returns.
The context stays.

Read the result in the same thread. Ask a follow-up in the saved session. If work is interrupted, inspect its state and explicitly choose how to recover.

!resultRetrieve a saved answer without running the model again.

Good to know before you go.
01
Is this a hosted AI service?
No. plompy-engine is MIT-licensed software you run yourself on Linux. You provide the machine, Discord bot and model access. A VPS is one way to host it; third-party services may have their own costs. Coding CLIs run on your host; model requests may go to an external provider.
02
Can I use any of the three coding agents?
Codex is the default. Claude Code and OpenCode adapters are experimental and have different execution boundaries. Supervised goals and still-image input currently require Codex. The published Docker image includes Codex only.
03
What happens if something stops?
Accepted work and results have durable state. Interrupted work remains visible for inspection and explicit recovery; uncertain external actions are not automatically replayed. Messages sent during a full outage may not have entered the queue. The public edition uses one shared worker.
